## Rule

ARC-GEN source `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_b27ca6d3.py`: input hides green cells as black. Red
horizontal/vertical domino centers are the anchors; output restores green on the union of the two
3x3 neighborhoods around each red domino, while preserving the red centers. Isolated red pixels
remain red distractions.

## Algorithm sketch

```
red = (input == 2)
has_orthogonal_red_neighbor = conv4(red) > 0
cluster = red & has_orthogonal_red_neighbor
green = maxpool3(cluster) & active_grid & ~red
output = background_onehot(active_grid & ~red & ~green) + red_onehot(red) + green_onehot(green)
```

Current best crops only ch0 to the generator-native 18x18 bound. It infers the active rectangle
with row/column `ReduceMax`, feeds `[active, ch0]` into a biased QLinearConv that emits
`[ch0, domino]`, then uses a final QLinearConv as the graph output. The final painter uses
`y_zero_point=1`, `y_scale=3`: positives accumulate in `[-1,1]` and negatives are `<= -2`, producing
exact 1/0 one-hot channels while dropping the explicit red feature plane.

## Cost analysis

Live cost 20,348 is dominated by rebuilding a full `[1,10,18,18]` one-hot `output_inner` (6,480 B)
plus repeated 18x18 F16 planes. The #67 value-canvas rewrite removes the 10-channel explosion but
must sentinel off-active cells inside the 18x18 crop, and measured worse than the final-Where
substitution route: 8,732 vs 5,491.

Current staged `ch0_domino_qpaint_noaxes` cost 3,517 = memory 3,276 + params 241. It is the
3,518 `nosteps` graph with the Slice axes omitted; ONNX defaults axes to `[0,1,2,3]`, so full
starts/ends cost 8 params instead of starts+ends+axes cost 9. Charged memory is unchanged:
- ch0 crop F32 `[1,1,18,18]`: 1,296 B
- ch0_u8 `[1,1,18,18]`: 324 B
- active row/column masks `[1,1,18,1]` + `[1,1,1,18]`: 36 B
- active grid `[1,1,18,18]`: 324 B
- `[active,ch0]` concat `[1,2,18,18]`: 648 B
- feature tensor `[ch0,domino]` `[1,2,18,18]`: 648 B

The old 900 B `green30` condition is gone because the final QLinearConv writes the output directly
for free. The red F32 crop is also gone: inside the active rectangle, red is exactly `active - ch0`.
The explicit red U8 feature plane is gone too; the final painter recovers red from the local ch0
hole plus domino context with `y_zero_point=1`.

Kill-table after channel collapse:

| Paid tensor class | Bytes | Keep/drop verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| F32 ch0 crop | 1,296 | forced: one 2-D color read from the F32 input is unavoidable |
| ch0_u8 | 324 | forced: needed by row/col activity and by the final painter |
| active row/col masks | 36 | forced cheapest height/width gate; boundary leak is real |
| active grid | 324 | forced: feature QLinearConv needs full-cell active to derive red/domino at tails |
| `[active,ch0]` QLC input | 648 | forced: single `active+ch0` code can copy ch0 but cannot produce exact domino |
| `[ch0,domino]` final features | 648 | forced minimum final stack: all 1-channel painters fail; 2-channel `[ch0,domino]` is the only exact collapse found |

Sub-2000 would require the U8 stack to be about 700 B after the forced 1,296 B F32 crop. The current
minimum exact U8 stack is 1,980 B (`324+36+324+648+648`), so the defensible floor for this graph
family is about 3.3k memory plus params. Confirmed nibble savings are default Slice steps (-3 params)
and default Slice axes (-1 param). Direct raw-input final Conv was probed as a local linear threshold
family over 3x3/4x4/5x5/7x7 red patches and is not linearly separable on the bundled corpus
(green/background conflicts/errors). A 2026-06-24 fused final-kernel probe over `[active,ch0]`
confirmed red is separable, but green/black are not: 5x5 and 7x7 linear SVC probes had 6,205 and
6,085 official+arc-gen cell errors respectively.

## Don't-do log

- **Crop 17×18 or 18×17**: Training max is 17×18 but live data requires exactly 18×18 (both dimensions). All asymmetric crops fail verify.
- **fp16_selective**: spread scan shows +16560 bytes regression — do not apply.
- **crop_to_size_advisory (naive)**: advisory says ~23k savings. The actual crop is already at 18×18 which the live data needs. The advisory was measuring the 30×30 model INPUT (excluded from cost), not an internal intermediate. The real intermediate to eliminate is input_inner via ReduceMax trick (done above).
- **Ungated positive-bias final Conv**: free-output Conv is valid only with negative/no-leak padding behavior. Do not use a positive bias or a green formula that can fire from cluster taps outside the active grid; gate edge cases and full A/B.
- **#67 value-canvas as primary**: fully gated but costs 8,732 after the required active-sentinel base canvas; `Where(green30, green_onehot, input)` is strictly cheaper for this sparse-substitution rule.
- **Direct raw-input linear Conv**: local 3x3 feature conflicts and 5x5/7x7 linear probes fail on bundled pairs; the green predicate is pairwise/nonlinear, not a single local threshold over red pixels.
- **No-active pair stamps**: cheap at 3,897 but visible 182/265; pair stamps leak past variable width/height tails.
- **Dynamic native Slice/Pad**: visible-correct but not scoreable (`score_network_v2` and real-input profile return None). Do not stage as a safe candidate.
- **Sparse-score non-one-hot output**: visible 0/265. The harness uses `np.array_equal` against encoded one-hot tensors; decoded argmax-only outputs are not accepted.
- **Drop final red feature without `y_zp=1`**: `[ch0,domino]` is sign-separable but not exact one-hot under normal `y_zero_point=0`; use the staged `y_zp=1`, `y_scale=3` version.
- **Final painter 1-channel or wrong 2-channel subsets**: formal unique-feature checks over `{active,ch0,red,domino}` show conflicts/infeasible exact-bin constraints. Only `[ch0,domino]` survived.
- **Feature QLinearConv from ch0 alone or active+ch0 code alone**: ch0-only has red/domino feature conflicts; `active+ch0` can copy ch0 but cannot produce exact domino. Keep `[active,ch0]`.
- **Omit QLinearConv zero points**: the checker rejects empty-string zero-point inputs for this QLinearConv schema (`input 2 is marked single`), so `x_zp`/`w_zp` are still required params.
